hero.title: Control the Windows desktop
hero.lede: Arrange monitors, place windows, set wallpapers and switch audio, power, radios and devices. Use the tray app with hotkeys and rules, or automate the same things from PowerShell, C#, the command line or an AI agent.

art.caption: Design mockup of the Monitors page. Not a shipped screen.

controls.title: What it controls
controls.lede: Each area below ships today in the PowerShell module and the .NET library. The names under each card are real cmdlets you can run.

areas.title: Monitors and layout
areas.body: List monitors, move them on the virtual desktop, change resolution and orientation, and set brightness. Save the whole setup as a workstation profile and restore it later.

areas.title: Windows
areas.body: Find windows by title or process, then move, resize, snap, keep on top or fade them. Save a window layout and put every window back later.

areas.title: UI automation
areas.body: Read the controls inside a window through Win32 or UI Automation, then click, type and check values directly. Wait for a window or control to appear instead of sleeping.

areas.title: Wallpaper and lock screen
areas.body: Set a different wallpaper on each monitor from a file, URL or stream. Run and step slideshows, keep a wallpaper history and set the lock screen image.

areas.title: Taskbar and personalization
areas.body: Find each taskbar and the monitor it sits on, move or hide it and switch auto-hide. Save a personalization snapshot before you change a theme.

areas.title: Audio
areas.body: List playback and recording devices with volume, mute and default roles. Change the default device for each role and react when a device appears or changes.

areas.title: Power and session
areas.body: Read battery and session state, lock or sign out, sleep or hibernate, and keep the machine and display awake for a set time.

areas.title: Wi-Fi and radios
areas.body: Turn Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and mobile broadband radios on or off through the supported Windows radio API. Connect a saved Wi-Fi profile without scanning or reading credentials.
areas.note: Global airplane mode is experimental and needs -Experimental.

areas.title: Devices and drivers
areas.body: List Plug and Play devices and the ones with problems. Enable, disable or restart a device, update its driver and manage Driver Store packages.

areas.title: Virtual desktops
areas.body: Check which virtual desktop a window is on and move it to another desktop through the public Windows API.
areas.note: Listing, creating, renaming and switching desktops are not supported.

areas.title: Screenshots and input
areas.body: Capture every monitor, one monitor, a region or a single window. Move and click the mouse, drag, scroll, press keys and read or set clipboard text.

areas.title: Hotkeys and events
areas.body: Bind a global hotkey to a PowerShell script block. Run code when monitors, resolution, orientation, the session, audio devices or radios change.

ways.title: Four ways to use it
ways.lede: The app, the cmdlets, the CLI and the MCP server all sit on one C# library, so a window move or a wallpaper change behaves the same way wherever you start it.

app.title: Tray app with hotkeys and layout rules
app.body: A Windows app for daily use at your own desk. It has no installer release yet; build it from the repository.
items: Tray icon, start with Windows and start minimized to the tray
Global hotkeys that maximize or restore the active window, or move it to the left half, the right half or an exact rectangle on a chosen monitor
Layout rules that match windows by title and process name, applied on demand or when the app starts
HDR on or off for each monitor
A Desktop state tab for workstation profiles, audio, keep-awake, taskbar auto-hide, radios and virtual desktops

surfaces.title: 133 cmdlets for scripts and admin work
surfaces.body: Run them by hand, in scheduled tasks or in deployment scripts. Works in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.
surfaces.code:
Get-DesktopMonitor -ConnectedOnly | Format-Table
Set-DesktopWallpaper -Index 1 -WallpaperPath 'C:\Wallpapers\wide.jpg' -Position Fit
Set-DesktopWindowSnap -Name '*Notepad*' -Position Left

Save-DesktopWorkstationProfile -Name 'office'
Restore-DesktopWorkstationProfile -Name 'office' -Confirm

Register-DesktopHotkey -Key F12 -Modifiers Control,Alt -Action { Lock-DesktopSession }

surfaces.title: The DesktopManager NuGet package
surfaces.body: Put the same engine inside your own app or service. Targets .NET Framework 4.7.2, .NET Standard 2.0, .NET 8 and .NET 10.

surfaces.title: A command line, and an MCP server for AI agents
surfaces.body: desktopmanager.exe returns plain text or JSON. desktopmanager mcp serve gives an agent more than 100 tools over stdio. It starts read-only: changing windows, changing system settings and experimental features each need their own switch, and --dry-run previews a change without making it.

download.label: Portable CLI and MCP bundle on GitHub Releases

surfaces.code:
desktopmanager monitor list --json
desktopmanager window snap --process notepad --position left
desktopmanager layout save coding
desktopmanager layout apply coding --validate

desktopmanager mcp serve
desktopmanager mcp serve --allow-mutations --allow-process notepad
desktopmanager mcp serve --dry-run

pbg.title: The engine behind PowerBGInfo wallpapers
pbg.body: PowerBGInfo draws the facts; DesktopManager puts them on screen. PowerBGInfo uses the DesktopManager package to apply its wallpapers to each monitor, to the lock screen and to every user profile.
